title: Crispy Fish Tacos with Garlic-Lime Crema
subtitle: golden panko cod in warm tortillas with a honey-lime slaw, corn, cheese and a cool garlic-lime crema
imageAlt: Soft flour tortillas filled with golden panko fish strips, shredded slaw, corn, cheese, diced tomato and avocado with a drizzle of white crema and lime wedges on a cream plate beside a navy napkin
servingsNote: 8 tacos: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus lunches

breakdown: Seaquest wild Pacific cod, 600 g (2 × 400 g bags at $7.50)

beforeYouStart.text: Thaw the frozen cod in the fridge overnight, or sealed in cold water 30–45 minutes, then pat it very dry.
Make the crema and slaw first so they chill while the fish bakes.

items.name: frozen wild Pacific cod fillets
items.note: about 1½ bags (400 g each), thawed, patted very dry, cut in 2.5 cm (1 in) strips

items.name: mild taco seasoning
items.note: our Mild Taco Seasoning or store-bought mild

steps.title: Crema and slaw
steps.text: Stir the sour cream, mayonnaise, lime juice, grated garlic and salt until smooth. In another bowl, toss the coleslaw mix with the 1 tbsp lime juice, honey and a pinch of salt. Chill both.

steps.title: Set up
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F) and set a rack on a lined baking sheet. Pat the fish very dry. Mix the flour with the taco seasoning in one shallow dish, beat the eggs in a second, and toss the panko with the oil in a third.

steps.title: Coat
steps.text: Dredge each strip in the flour, dip in the egg, then press into the panko on all sides. Lay on the rack in one layer, not touching.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 12–14 minutes, flipping once halfway, until golden and crisp and the thickest strip reads 70°C (158°F) and flakes easily.

steps.title: Warm the rest
steps.text: While the fish bakes, microwave the corn covered 1–2 minutes, then warm the tortillas in a dry skillet over medium, 20–30 seconds a side, and keep them wrapped in a clean towel.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Fill each tortilla with slaw, 2–3 fish strips, cheese, corn, tomato and avocado. Drizzle with crema and serve with lime wedges.

fixIt.fix: Dry the fish well and press the panko on firmly; flip gently with tongs.
Spray or drizzle a little more oil on top and give it 2 more minutes.
Warm them right before serving and keep them wrapped in a towel.

saleTip: Seaquest Wild Pacific Cod Fillets are $7.50 for a 400 g bag at No Frills. Buy 2 bags; the extra 200 g keeps frozen for next taco night.
swap: Haddock or pollock: same timing. Basa is the cheapest swap but softer: handle it gently and check it at 10 minutes. Plain shredded cabbage for the coleslaw mix. Store-bought mild taco seasoning works if you're out of ours.
leftovers: Keep the fish, slaw and crema apart. Re-crisp the fish and make fresh tacos, or have it on a rice bowl.
doneness: Fish at 70°C (158°F): opaque and flakes easily (Health Canada, fish).
source: Based on tested baked panko fish taco methods (Canadian Living, Budget Bytes): flour-egg-panko coated fish strips baked hot on a rack, a sour cream lime crema and a quick lime slaw. No chili or hot sauce.
prepAhead: Make the crema up to 3 days ahead.
Mix the slaw up to 4 hours ahead.
Cut the fish and keep it covered in the fridge up to a day ahead.
reheat: Fish on a rack at 200°C (400°F) for 5–6 minutes, or in the air fryer for 3–4 minutes, until 74°C (165°F). Crema and slaw are served cold.
airFryer: Air-fry the coated strips in one layer, in batches, at 200°C (400°F) for 8–10 minutes, flipping once, until golden and 70°C (158°F) inside. Spray the tops with cooking spray first.

basic.note: Crispy fish tacos with plain slaw, cheese, corn and the crema; no slaw dressing, tomato or avocado.

stepNotes.0: Basic: skip the slaw dressing; use the coleslaw mix plain.

fancy.note: A fresh mango salsa on top and smoked paprika in the crema.

stepNotes.0: Fancy: stir the smoked paprika into the crema.
stepNotes.5: Fancy: spoon mango salsa over each taco.

addSteps.title: Mango salsa
addSteps.text: Toss the mango, red onion and lime juice. Chill until serving.

plating: Three tacos standing in a row.
Mango salsa and a zigzag of crema on top.
Lime wedges and extra crema on the side.

why.0-4: Panko tossed with oil bakes up crunchy without frying.
why.1-2: Lime in the crema and slaw keeps the tacos bright.
why.0-2: Our mild taco blend seasons the coating with no heat.

funFact: Fish tacos come from Baja California, where battered fish in tortillas became a street-stand staple in Ensenada in the 1950s.

keeps.note: cooked fish loses its crunch when frozen; keep the crema and slaw separate

drink: Sparkling water with lime, or a cold Mexican lager.
